notes:
Four-part task on the register vocabulary and the C7 census (brief: untracked/T269-register-vocabulary.md; read-order: AGENTS.md, DELEGATEE.md, DIRECTION.md, brief). Scope: C7 machinery + vocabulary proposal + findings-schema adjudication paths. T272 (absorbed-with-rejection) and T280 (gate) were already done when I claimed; T284 landed mid-session (floor restored: C1a=10, C2=14, C6=0; gate reinstalled) — I verified no overlap with claimlint.

PART 1 — 'not a register claim' disposition (T264-V1/V2/V3). Implemented by EXTENDING the T272 rejection registry rather than a second mechanism: entries now carry a disposition (rejected-by-register | not-a-register-claim | absorbed-under-register-id) and the reason is MANDATORY. loadRejections refuses reason-less not-a-register-claim entries, refuting-row-less rejected-by-register entries and refuting-row-less absorbed-under-register-id entries; refused entries are reported as INVALID and do NOT silence (calibrated: known-bad 10). T264-V1/V2/V3 are dispositioned not-a-register-claim with per-row reasons. T265 (in T267-key-agreement.json and T267-context.json) is dispositioned absorbed-under-register-id → CODE.GTP-KOKEY (PROVEN), because the findings files used the task ID as the claim ID; the proposal matches the row the content was absorbed under.

PART 2 — 'true when written, overtaken by events'. Proposed and implemented a first-class status SUPERSEDED (enum + parseStatus + name; neither live nor false, so C1a/C3/B skip it and no falsification travels through it; added to shadowedEdges' can-never-be-FALSE set; added to the findings schema in findings/README.md and docs/infra/agents/findings-schema.json). Applied to exactly the two rows the brief named: CODE.WZO2-UNRUN and CODE.WZO2-CHAINSHORT. The two PROGRESS.md cite-tags were updated to match ([CODE.WZO2-UNRUN:SUPERSEDED], [CODE.WZO2-CHAINSHORT:SUPERSEDED]) so C6 stays 0. C3 debt list 78 → 76: the two rows stop claiming PROVEN, which is the point of the status. Chose a coded status over an annotation convention because the register itself documented the gap ('The register has no status for true when written, obsolete now') and prose annotations already rotted once (CHAINSHORT was never annotated despite T261 knowing the fix).

PART 3 — the C7 parse defects (T266, two independent seats). Rewrote parseFindingsFile on std.json (no more char scan): every new_rows entry is read, every status is parsed correctly. Effect (command: `bin/weizigo-claimlint`): new-rows touched 4 → 16, claims touched 25 → 42, unabsorbed 7 → 2. Invisible rows: 12 new_rows (3 from T266-incompleteness rows 2-4, 4 from T279-absorption rows 2-5, 5 string-form rows from T279-context that the old parser could not see at all) and 17 claim items (string-form context-dump claims + T283's two files). Of the invisible new_rows, T266's three were absorbed by T279 only because T266's own notes told the absorber to read the file directly — the census gap was real. New calibration: a two-row new_rows fixture (known-bad 8) that fails on the old parser (it counted 1 row and mis-parsed the status) and passes on the fix; also fixed a latent calibration weakness where extra synthetic register rows were grafted AFTER the ## 3. end footer and never parsed (known-bad 6 was passing for the wrong reason — NO SUCH ID instead of a real status mismatch).

PART 4 — C7 silently skipped non-conforming files. Now REPORTED: 7 of 66 files are non-conforming and are listed with the reason (T258-fleet top-level array; T259-m4b, T260-fleet-triage, T261-m4b-triage, T263-clearcapacity, T265-ko-key-mismatch, T271-axioms missing required keys). They are pre-schema records (some cited as evidence by PROVEN rows), so they are reported but do not fail the run; the count is in the summary for the floor mechanism to ratchet. Calibrated (known-bad 9).

RELATED — worth proposing not building: no check compares a PROVEN row against evidence that arrived after the row was written; a cheap 'is the cited file newer than the row's last edit?' check would have flagged the four rows that went stale in one day. Deliberately not built (the brief says propose, and mtimes on a moving checkout are a weak signal); filed as a future C8 idea.

LIVE LEAK, NOT MINE TO CLOSE: C7 ends at 2 unabsorbed — `T267` in T267-key-agreement.json and T267-context.json. The finding (producer/consumer key-agreement invariant wired into zig build test, proposed PROVEN) is real and has NO register row: CODE.GTP-KOKEY still lists the invariant as owed. The ID is the task ID, not a claim ID, so it cannot be mechanically absorbed. Absorption (mint a row, verify-then-promote — the suite passing is not the same as an independent seat) is a separate task; I did not do it because the brief's deliverables are the vocabulary and the census, and T267's own dump honestly flags untested corners (2x2 seeded-defect may pass vacuously; 4x4 self-play may not have reached a ko).

WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH: whether the Orchestrator wants C7 non-conforming to eventually FAIL the run (I report, don't fail — the 7 are immutable pre-schema records); whether the 2 remaining unabsorbed T267 items are acceptable until an absorption task lands.

WHAT I NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON: (1) T267's T265-claim duplicates across two findings files — both dispositioned, so C7 is quiet, but the duplicate itself is a schema-hygiene smell; (2) findings/README.md and findings-schema.json are both edited for SUPERSEDED — they must not diverge; (3) the old C7 char scanner also mis-handled T279-absorption's claims (id+rationale, no proposed_status) — the new presence-check semantics handle them, but those records are arguably not findings at all.
